title: Dynamic TMoE: A Drift-Aware Dynamic Mixture of Experts Framework for Non-Stationary Time Series Forecasting
claim: Conventional approaches use static routing and fixed homogeneous components that fail under distribution shift; ours uses memory-aware routing and a dynamic heterogeneous pool.
layout: 2 stacked panels; (b) split left/right by dashed line, top-to-bottom flow
description: Panel (a) at the top shows a time series on a timeline, split into blue, orange and green segments at t1, t2 and t3. Beneath each segment is a small filled distribution curve in the matching color, labeled 'Distribution Shift'. Arrows lead from the three distributions into panel (b), a dashed box divided vertically into two halves. The left half, 'Conventional MoE', has a Static Router above three identical hard-hat worker icons labeled homogeneous experts, with a pin icon and the label 'Fixed Expert Pool'. The right half, 'Dynamic TMoE', has a Temporal Memory Router with a recurrent hidden-state loop. It sits above three different worker icons with a refresh icon and the label 'Dynamic Expert Pool'. Below each half is a True vs Pred forecast plot. The left shows a sad face, 'Inability to Adapt to Drift', and mismatched predictions. The right shows a happy face, 'Dynamic Drift Adaptation', and predictions that track the truth closely. The eye goes first to the colored waveform at the top, then to the side-by-side contrast.
caption: (a) Time series data with distribution shift. (b) Comparison between Conventional MoE and Dynamic TMoE. Conventional MoE: Limited by static routing and fixed homogeneous experts, struggling to adapt to distribution shifts. Dynamic TMoE: Employs temporal memory routing and a dynamic heterogeneous pool for history-aware, specialized adaptation.
abstract: Non-stationary time series forecasting is challenged by evolving distribution shifts that static models struggle to capture. While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising paradigm for decoupling complex drift patterns, existing approaches are limited by fixed expert pools and memoryless routing, hampering their ability to adapt to abrupt regime shifts. To address this, we propose Dynamic TMoE, a framework that unifies architectural evolution with temporal continuity during learning phase. By detecting distribution shifts via Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), we dynamically instantiate heterogeneous experts and prune redundant ones to optimize capacity. Additionally, a temporal memory router leverages recurrent states and an anomaly repository to ensure stable, context-aware expert selection without requiring test-time updates. Experiments on nine benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, reducing MSE by 10.4% and MAE by 7.8%. Code is available at https://github.com/andone-07/Dynamic-TMoE.
